title: One Walk, Seven Centuries
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Walk downhill through Ephesus monument by monument, predicting whether each was begun before or after the one just passed, and watch the timeline zigzag across seven centuries.

educational.topic: The Monuments of Ephesus in Time
learningObjectives: Compare the construction dates of nine monuments passed on the downhill walk through Ephesus, predicting for each one whether it was begun before or after the monument passed just before it, with at least 6 of 8 predictions correct.
prerequisites: The Memmius Monument and Curetes Street
The Gate of Hercules and the Fountain of Trajan
The Temple of Hadrian and the terrace houses
The Library of Celsus and the Gate of Mazaeus and Mithridates
The Great Theater and the Harbor Street

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal comparison: commit to older or younger before each date appears, then read the finished timeline as layers
keyQuestions: Walking downhill, is the next monument older or younger?
Does the walk run steadily from older to newer?
Which monuments already stood when Paul was in Ephesus?
commonMisconceptions: A site is built in one period, so neighboring monuments are about the same age.
The downhill walk runs steadily from older to newer, or the reverse.
A monument's construction date is the date of everything in it; the Gate of Hercules reuses older carved blocks, and the theater was rebuilt over several centuries.
assessmentOpportunities: Correct predictions out of eight (mastery: 6 of 8).
Correct a guide's claim that everything on Curetes Street is 2nd-century Roman, using three monuments.
